issues.legal_issue: An allottee who accepts delayed delivery of a house at the agreed price and receives the benefit of the property's appreciation is not entitled to interest on the amount paid for the period before delivery.
material_facts: The allottee's payment for the houses was adjusted from money refundable for other units, and the price of the houses was treated as paid on the date of that adjustment.
The houses were delivered years later at the agreed prices, and the allottee accepted delivery.
The Commission awarded interest at a uniform rate without a proper basis for its commencement date.
The value of the houses had increased substantially by the time they were delivered.
issues.conclusion: The interest award was unsustainable. Because the houses were delivered and accepted at the agreed prices, the allottee was not entitled to interest on the price paid for the period before delivery.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principles in Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta, Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh, Haryana Development Authority v. Darsh Kumar, and Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Union of India, relief for delayed delivery depends on the circumstances and cannot be based on an automatic, uniform interest rate. Where delayed performance is accepted at the agreed price and the allottee benefits from appreciation in value, interest on the price paid until delivery does not arise.

predicates.consumer_complaint_for_delayed_housing_a: An allottee brought a consumer complaint alleging delay in delivery of an allotted house.
predicates.delayed_houses_were_delivered_and_accept: The housing authority delivered the delayed houses and the allottee accepted them at the agreed prices.
predicates.allottee_benefited_from_property_appreci: The value of the houses had increased by the time the allottee received them.

issues.definition: When an allottee brings a consumer complaint over delayed housing delivery, accepts the houses at the agreed prices, and benefits from their appreciation, the rule denies interest on the paid price until delivery.

issues.legal_issue: A claimed rental loss is not established by an affidavit alone when documentary evidence of the rent was available but not produced.
material_facts: The allottee claimed compensation for rent allegedly paid for replacement houses during the delay.
The allottee did not produce documents showing payment of rent or evidence of the prevailing rent for similar houses.
The allottee did not claim that documentary evidence of the rent was unavailable.
issues.conclusion: The claimed rental loss could not be used as a basis for awarding damages because the available documentary evidence was not produced and an affidavit statement alone was insufficient.
issues.legal_principle: Where documentary evidence supporting a claimed loss is available but is not produced, a bare statement in an affidavit is not sufficient to establish damages.

rule.if: delayed_housing_allotment_compensation_claim and rental_loss_is_claimed and rental_documents_were_available and rental_documents_were_not_produced and rent_was_supported_only_by_affidavit

predicates.delayed_housing_allotment_compensation_c: An allottee claimed compensation in a proceeding concerning delayed delivery of a house.
predicates.rental_loss_is_claimed: The allottee claimed to have incurred rent because the allotted house was not delivered on time.
predicates.rental_documents_were_available: Documents capable of showing the rent paid or the prevailing rent were available to the allottee.
predicates.rental_documents_were_not_produced: The allottee did not produce those rental documents.
predicates.rent_was_supported_only_by_affidavit: The claimed rent was supported only by a statement in an affidavit.

issues.definition: When an allottee claims rental loss from delayed housing delivery but leaves available rental documents unproduced and relies only on an affidavit, the claimed rental loss is not established.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation for delayed housing delivery is not warranted where the allottee did not establish negligence or deficiency by the authority and the surrounding circumstances do not show an actionable failure in performance.
material_facts: The scheme materials and the parties' agreement did not specify a delivery date, and the scheme's payment instalments were not paid when due by the allottee.
The authority's letter mentioning an expected completion date also set out instalments that the allottee did not pay.
The authority received the price by adjustment only later and delivered some houses before the remaining houses were delayed by the contractor's work stoppage and dispute.

The authority tried to persuade the contractor to resume work, sought government intervention, cancelled the contractor's agreement after those efforts failed, and completed the houses through another agency.
The allottee's earlier demands did not fix a reasonable time for performance or terminate the contract; its later notice demanded delivery within an unreasonable period.
The houses were eventually delivered at the agreed prices, and the allottee benefited from their increased value.
The allottee did not establish negligence by the authority.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances did not establish deficiency in service by the authority warranting compensation, and the allottee was not entitled to compensation for the delay.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principles summarized from Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta, Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh, Haryana Development Authority v. Darsh Kumar, and Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Union of India. In a construction contract, time is not the essence unless specified; where it is not the essence, a buyer who does not fix a reasonable time for performance or rescind cannot ordinarily claim damages for belated performance under general contract principles. Compensation under consumer law may nevertheless be available where a statutory authority acts negligently, arbitrarily, or capriciously. Whether compensation is justified depends on the facts, including the authority's reasons for delay, the allottee's conduct, and the nature of any proven harassment or loss.

predicates.consumer_complaint_for_delayed_housing_a: An allottee brought a consumer complaint alleging delayed delivery of an allotted house.
predicates.no_delivery_date_was_fixed: The scheme and agreement did not fix a delivery date.
predicates.allottee_did_not_pay_installments_when_d: The allottee failed to pay required instalments when they were due.
predicates.allottee_did_not_fix_a_reasonable_perfor: The allottee did not give the authority a reasonable deadline for performance before seeking compensation.
predicates.authority_took_steps_to_complete_work_af: After a contractor dispute delayed construction, the authority tried to resolve the problem and arranged for the work to be completed through another agency.
predicates.houses_were_delivered_at_agreed_price_an: The authority delivered the houses at the agreed prices, and the allottee benefited from their increased value.
predicates.authority_negligence_was_not_proved: The allottee did not establish that the authority acted negligently in performing its obligations.

issues.definition: When an allottee brings a delayed-housing consumer complaint, the delivery date was not fixed, the allottee did not pay instalments when due or set a reasonable performance deadline, the authority took steps to complete work delayed by a contractor dispute, the houses were delivered at the agreed price with appreciation benefiting the allottee, and authority negligence was not proved, compensation for the delay is not awarded.
